headline: Local Man Spends Six Months Polishing Voter ID Card Photo With Sandpaper To Ensure ‘More Professional’ Appearance
body:
Ramesh Kumar, a 34-year-old accountant from Hyderabad, has spent the last 180 days meticulously applying fine-grit sandpaper to his official state voter identification card, claiming the matte finish of the original print was 'insufficiently executive' for his upcoming trip to the polling booth.

Kumar, who has been documenting his progress on an Excel spreadsheet titled 'Optimizing Democratic Aesthetics,' stated he was inspired to begin the project after reading the draft electoral rolls for 2026. 'I looked at the record and realized my digital footprint didn't match the physical quality of the paper,' Kumar explained while buffing the corner of his card with a high-grade chamois cloth. 'A citizen’s proof of identity shouldn't just be a plastic sheet; it should be a tactile experience that commands respect when presented to the polling officer.'

Local election observers noted that while Kumar’s card is now significantly thinner and possesses a strange, translucent shimmer, the actual photograph has been reduced to a faint, unrecognizable smudge of ink. Kumar remains unfazed by the loss of clarity, noting that he is currently drafting a 40-page petition for the state election commission to allow voters to submit their own custom-printed, high-gloss identification cards featuring professional studio headshots.

'Democracy isn't just about the vote, it's about the presentation,' Kumar said, before attempting to spray a final layer of aerosolized lacquer over the now-unreadable barcode. 'If I’m going to stand in a queue for forty minutes, I want to make sure I’m holding something that looks like it belongs in a premium wallet, not a discarded gym membership.'
caption: When your electoral participation is more about the aesthetic than the actual act of voting. Ramesh is currently awaiting feedback on his request to add gold leaf to the margins. #VoterID #Elections2026 #CivicDuty (satire)
igHook: Tag someone who treats every piece of ID like it's a high-stakes business card.
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a pair of hands holding a piece of plastic ID card under a bright desk lamp, with various grades of fine sandpaper and polishing cloths scattered across a dark wooden table.

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 stands out because it targets a specific, relatable human neurosis (the obsession with 'professional' presentation) rather than just the tired 'registering pets as voters' trope present in half the other entries. The detail of the 40-page petition and the 'Optimizing Democratic Aesthetics' spreadsheet provides a vivid, specific image that feels fresh and authentically humorous.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a generic, fictional character to satirize over-preparation and bureaucracy. It does not target real individuals, religious or ethnic groups, and the image prompt is generic.
